title: Multi-tenant GPU slab imbalance + KV tombstone sweep runtime patch
creator: Marisol Chen
description: Production escalations observed across Hosted and Dedicated clusters where long-running multi-tenant sessions triggered GPU OOMs. Root cause analysis identified two interacting issues: allocator slab imbalance (causing persistent fragmentation on long-lived processes) and KV cache tombstone/handle retention that prevented reclamation. This ticket tracks the investigation, the runtime patch (compaction + KV tombstone sweep), rollout plan, and post-deploy verification.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Deploy workload that keeps large context sessions open for >12 hours with frequent soft evictions (prefix caching + long KV lifetimes).
2) Send high-concurrency small-batch traffic mixing short low-latency calls and long generation sessions to simulate tenant interleaving.
3) Observe GPU reserved memory growth with low usable contiguous blocks and increased allocation failures in metrics (alloc.fail, slab.free_ratio < 0.12).
4) Reproduce locally using dedicated test harness (gpu-sim-run) with synthetic KV churn for ~6-8 hours to see fragmentation pattern.
mitigation_actions: Immediate: Applied temporary routing rule in Hosted to steer suspicious sessions to dedicated low-priority nodes to reduce cross-tenant interference.
Immediate: Enabled hard LRU eviction for KV entries older than 24h in affected clusters (config flag).
Short term: Rolled patch to runtime that makes allocator expose a compaction trigger when fragmentation > threshold and runs an async compactor during low-load windows.
Short term: Implemented KV tombstone sweep that clears stale handles and consolidates free lists to avoid resident wasted pages.
Long term: Added model-level routing fallback (auto-route to smaller quantized variant) when node contiguous memory metrics fall below safety threshold.
decision_log: 2025-11-06: After heap profiles and nvprof sampling, engineering confirmed fragmentation stems from many small ephemeral allocations pinned by KV handles.
2025-11-07: Decided against immediate major allocator rewrite due to time; opted for targeted compaction + KV sweep to fix live clusters faster.
2025-11-09: QA validated compaction under synthetic 48h churn; KV sweep removed ~18% resident allocations on test nodes.
2025-11-12: Rollout strategy chosen: canary 2 nodes in hosted-realtime, canary 1 dedicated pool, observe 48h, then progressive 25/50/100% flips with 30-min health gates.

2025-11-14: Post-rollout: telemetry shows 92% reduction in alloc.fail alerts for affected pools and mean time-to-recovery for OOMs reduced from 11m to 90s due to faster reclamation and fallback routing.
qa_notes: Unit tests added for compactor trigger and KV sweep GC path.
Integration harness run: 72h continuous with mixed tenant load; no OOM and contiguous free ratio stayed >0.2 after compaction cycles.
Load test: Canary matched production percentiles for p50/p95 latency within 5% of baseline.
Regression checks: validated no increase in tail latency for short sessions and no KV correctness regressions in stored handles.
rollout_timeline: 2025-11-13 02:00 UTC: Canary on hosted-realtime (2 nodes) - pass health gates
2025-11-13 10:00 UTC: Canary on dedicated-pool-A (1 node) - pass
2025-11-17 12:00 UTC: Full verification and monitored for 48h; no regressions observed
postmortem_summary: Two interacting long-tail issues caused memory pressure to accumulate: allocator fragmentation from many small ephemeral GPU allocations and KV handles that left tombstones preventing reuse. The targeted runtime patch (on-demand compaction + KV tombstone sweep) addressed the immediate customer impact without a full allocator rewrite. Follow-ups include improved metrics for contiguous free blocks, stricter KV TTL defaults, and a quarterly stress test for multi-tenant fragmentation scenarios.
follow_up_actions: Implement continuous nightly compaction on low-load windows for dedicated pools (ENG-33845).
Run quarterly multi-tenant chaos tests that include long-lived sessions and KV churn (owner: reliability).
Add an alert: contiguous_free_ratio < 0.15 sustained for >30m triggers automated model fallback and paging policy.
Document guidance for customers: recommended KV TTLs and session patterns to avoid long-lived fragmentation.
Schedule design review for allocator redesign (Q1 2026) if compaction shows limits.
notes: Customer escalations came from two enterprise customers on Dedicated and three Hosted customers. We prioritized Dedicated pools due to SLA exposure.
We chose a low-risk path: small surface-area changes in the runtime with feature-flag gating to quickly rollback if needed.
Memory profiler outputs and example heap snapshots are saved in the Confluence doc linked above for future analysis.
